headline_seed: Pope Leo criticises Equatorial Guinea prisons as he winds up Africa tour
description_seed: The Pope gives a frank and passionate speech, the likes of which have characterised his tour of Africa.

what: Pope Leo criticises Equatorial Guinea prisons as he winds up Africa tour

clean_source_blocks.text: The Pope gives a frank and passionate speech, the likes of which have characterised his tour of Africa.
Oil-rich Equatorial Guinea, a country with a poor human rights record and vast income inequalities, is the Pope's final stop on a four-nation tour of Africa.

Equatorial Guinea's new generations, however, have struggled to make their voices heard: President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo is Africa's longest-serving president; his son, dubbed "little Teodoro," is vice president. At 83 years old, Obiang walked well while receiving Leo at the airport, using a cane to stand and his hand slightly trembling at his side.
Pope Leo has criticised the treatment of prisoners in Equatorial Guinea, ahead of a visit to a jail known for its dire conditions.
